paper_metadata.title: Temperature-dependent tensile behavior of the HfNbTaTiZr multi-principal element alloy

evidence.quote: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory multi-principal element alloy (RMPEA) that exhibits high strength combined with good ductility at room temperature.

parameters.time: 20 min pre-heat and 10 min re-heats between passes
parameters.deformation: reduced thickness by approximately 20% per pass, from 11 mm to 4 mm

evidence.quote: The button was inspected via X-ray radiography to confirm dissolution of the heavy elements, and then hot rolled into a sheet at 1150 ◦C in air with a 20 min pre-heat and 10 min re-heats between passes. The sheet thickness was reduced by approximately 20% per pass, from an initial thickness of 11 mm to a final thickness of 4 mm.
After hot rolling, the sheet was conditioned to remove surface cracks and defects and then vacuum annealed at 1100 ◦C for 1 h.

parameters.deformation: 3% reduction per pass to 2.5 mm, then 5% per pass to 1 mm

evidence.quote: Following annealing, the HfNbTaTiZr sheet was cold rolled at 3% reduction per pass down to 2.5 mm thick, then reduced by 5% thickness per pass down to 1 mm thick, with no cracking observed in the sheet.
Following cold rolling, the HfNbTaTiZr sheet was given a final recrystallization (RX) anneal under vacuum at 1100 ◦C for 1 h.

SEM and TEM studies revealed precipitation reactions at grain boundaries following thermal exposure and during tensile testing at 800 ◦C, resulting in tantalum and niobium-rich BCC precipitates, and finer-scale hafnium and zirconium-rich precipitates.
At 1200 ◦C, high tensile ductility resulted from the combined effects of dynamic recovery and partial dynamic recrystallization.

At 800 ◦C, the HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibited significantly decreased ductility (2.0%) compared to room temperature, and coincided with a transition from ductile to intergranular fracture.
